results.label: evicted-single
results.prompt: How do I list all evicted pods?

message.content:
To list all evicted pods in a specific namespace, you can use the following command:

```sh
kubectl get pods --field-selector status.phase=Evicted -n <namespace>
```

Replace `<namespace>` with the actual namespace name. This command filters pods based on their phase being `Evicted`.

If you want to list evicted pods across all namespaces, you can use:

```sh
kubectl get pods --field-selector status.phase=Evicted -A
```

This command uses the `-A` flag to list resources across all namespaces.

To list evicted pods using `oc`, the OpenShift client, you can use:

```sh
oc get pods --field-selector status.phase=Evicted -n <namespace>
```

Again, replace `<namespace>` with the actual namespace name. The `-A` flag is not available in `oc`, so you must specify the namespace explicitly.

These commands will help you identify and manage evicted pods in your OpenShift or Kubernetes cluster.

results.label: concurrent-rollout
results.prompt: How do I check deployment rollout status and view logs in namespace demo? Include oc and kubectl examples.

message.content:
To check the rollout status of a deployment and view logs in the `demo` namespace, you can use the following commands:

### Using `kubectl`
```sh
kubectl rollout status deployment/<deployment-name> -n demo
kubectl logs <pod-name> -n demo
```

### Using `oc`
```sh
oc rollout status deployment/<deployment-name> -n demo
oc logs <pod-name> -n demo
```

### Explanation
- **`kubectl rollout status deployment/<deployment-name> -n demo`**: This command checks the status of the rollout for the specified deployment in the `demo` namespace. Replace `<deployment-name>` with the actual name of your deployment.
- **`kubectl logs <pod-name> -n demo`**: This command retrieves the logs for the specified pod in the `demo` namespace. Replace `<pod-name>` with the actual name of your pod.

### Prerequisites
- Ensure you have `kubectl` or `oc` installed and configured to access your Kubernetes cluster.
- Ensure you have the necessary permissions to view deployments and logs in the `demo` namespace.
- Install `jq` if you need to filter logs or other JSON data.

### Notes
- Replace `<deployment-name>` and `<pod-name>` with the actual names of your deployment and pod.
- If you want to view logs for all pods in a deployment, you can use:
  ```sh
  kubectl logs -l app=<app-label> -n demo
  ```
  Replace `<app-label>` with the appropriate label for your deployment.
